subject: Network onramp and control/data ownership for private inference deployment
messages:
From: Sara Hayes <sara.hayes@acmehealth.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: cloudops@edgehost.com
Date: Thu, 07 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Private inference edge deployment — network onramp + ownership questions

Hi Olga / Irene,

Thanks for taking this on. We’re starting the engineering evaluation for a private, customer-managed VPC deployment of Redwood inference nodes for our EU-based inference cluster. The goals are: minimal cross-account egress, strict control-plane isolation, and an automated onramp for tenant onboarding.

Attached are the initial topology sketches and a short procurement spreadsheet listing expected capacity and compliance constraints. High-level asks:
- Can Redwood operate the control plane (control signals, model management) in a dedicated VPC peered to our environment, or must the control plane be customer-managed inside our VPC for compliance?
- How do you recommend handling data-plane egress for telemetry when we cannot allow any tokenized payload to cross public networks?
- What minimal connectivity (ports, FQDNs, IP ranges) do your edge agents require for initial bootstrap and updates?

We’re aiming to kick off a short architecture review this week and would like a 45-minute sync with the Redwood infra/ops owners. Proposed times below.

Attachments: acme-infra-drawings.pdf, acme-procurement-q3.xlsx

Thanks,
Sara Hayes
Head of Platform, Acme HealthTech

From: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Hayes <sara.hayes@acmehealth.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 07 Sep 2028 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private inference edge deployment — network onramp + ownership questions

Sara — thanks for the detailed brief and attachments, this is exactly the right level to start. I booked a slot (Fri 09:00 UTC) on the calendar you suggested; if that doesn’t work I’ll send alternatives.

Quick answers up front so your procurement/security folks have something concrete: 
- Control plane ownership: we support both models. The most common for regulated workloads is customer-managed control plane inside a private VPC (we provide an installable control-plane package and an optional small management tunnel for telemetry, both over mTLS). If you need Redwood to operate the control plane, we can run it from a dedicated account/VPC with strict egress allowlists and per-tenant encryption keys, but that requires a PSA and higher SLA alignment.
- Data-plane telemetry: we can ship telemetry via an outbound-only, token-less metrics/aggregates channel (TLS to Redwood ingest endpoints) or you can configure a local telemetry aggregator (Prometheus pushgateway / pull via private interconnect) so no PII/tokenized content leaves your network.
- Bootstrap connectivity: outbound HTTPS (443) to a short allowlist of FQDNs + IP ranges, and mTLS on a configurable port for control-plane registration. I pasted the minimal list below and will convert to an allowlist CSV for procurement.

Minimal allowlist (summary):
- outbound: telemetry.redwood.ai (443), updates.redwood.ai (443)
- inbound: optional mTLS registration port 8443 from your bootstrap host(s)
- management: DNS, NTP for node time sync (recommend internal NTP)

We’ll discuss the control/data ownership tradeoffs in the sync; I’ve asked Irene for a short reference diagram that shows our recommended demarcation patterns (control-plane inside customer VPC vs managed-control-plane).

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Hayes <sara.hayes@acmehealth.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 07 Sep 2028 12:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private inference edge deployment — network onramp + ownership questions

Olga / Sara — adding a few technical constraints I want noted before the call: 

1) Control-plane data separation: model artifacts, rollout signals, and metrics are separate flows. For customer-managed control plane we recommend storing model artifacts in a customer-controlled object store (S3-compatible with KMS keys) and pointing the runtime to that bucket. That avoids artifact egress to Redwood-managed storage.

2) KV cache & ephemeral state: the inference nodes keep KV cache locally; we do not replicate raw prompt history off-host unless configured for observability. If Acme requires centralized session replay for QA, we suggest an internal sidecar that scrubs tokens and ships only hashed traces.

3) Firmware/updates: the node updater will check updates.redwood.ai over HTTPS. If updates must be pulled from an internal mirror, we can provide a signed artifacts feed and a small mirror tool.

I’ve sketched two reference demarcation diagrams and uploaded them to the Drive link Olga pasted. Will present the diagrams in the review and highlight where a DMZ or private egress proxy is recommended.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Sara Hayes <sara.hayes@acmehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 08 Sep 2028 09:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private inference edge deployment — network onramp + ownership questions

Couple of operational notes I’ll cover in the sync: 
- Canary control-plane models: recommend canary and fallback variants that are pinned within the customer VPC for critical paths; if the managed control plane is used, we need a mutual-fallback plan that fails safe to a local runtime stub.
- Observability egress: suggest a two-path setup — metrics -> agg (no tokens), and trace/logs -> local aggregator that implements a token scrub policy. We also support sampling rules to limit PII risk.
- ACLs & BGP: for sites using direct interconnects we can accept a BGP advertisement for dedicated prefixes; otherwise, an egress NAT with strict SNAT per tenant is fine.

I attached a short checklist I use for handoffs (I’ll paste the checklist output into the Drive doc as well). Looking forward to reviewing today.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Site Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

I’ll drop the procurement contact (Marek Kowalski) into the Jira ticket and share his contact if you need kickoff on logistics.
